subtitle: Cross-reference of September 15, 2026, reading of Sep 15, 14:44 BRT (17:44 UTC), with the presidential book at USD 149.89M. Four of the five monitored contracts received a new price in this round: winner, first-round runner-up, Supreme Court impeachment and Senate. The first-round third-place contract had no new reading on Sep 15 and keeps the values of Sep 14. On the polling side, two national polls were released today: Indexa/Broadcast, fieldwork from Sep 10 to 13, 2,000 telephone interviews, margin of 2.2pp, register BR-03482/2026 at the Superior Electoral Court; and CNT/MDA, fieldwork from Sep 9 to 13, 2,002 in-person interviews, same margin, register BR-06902/2026. Both put Lula ahead in both rounds and disagree on the magnitude: 1 point of distance in the runoff in one and 7.3 points in the other.

candidates.name: Lula
candidates.header: PRICE: 46.50% (vol USD 11.11M accumulated) in the winner contract, reading of Sep 15, 14:44 BRT, up 1.00pp against the price confirmed on Sep 14, interrupting two straight days of losses. POLLS: 38% in the first round and 43% in the runoff against Flávio Bolsonaro in Indexa/Broadcast of Sep 15, and 40.5% and 47.3% in CNT/MDA of the same day.
fortes: He leads the first round in both national polls of Sep 15, by 38% to 34% in Indexa/Broadcast and by 40.5% to 30.4% in CNT/MDA, and both distances fall outside two margins of 2.2.
He also leads all five runoff pairs in both houses, and in CNT/MDA he wins all five outside two margins.
In the winner contract he rises 1.00pp, to 46.50%, and the gap to the front-runner narrows from 6.45pp to 5.15pp.
fracos: He remains behind in the winner contract, with 46.50% against 51.65% for Flávio Bolsonaro.
His price sits 21.00pp below the series high, of 67.50% on Aug 16, and the distance to that high did not narrow materially in this round.
In the first-round runner-up contract he falls 1.90pp, to 21.85%, the largest single move among the contracts that received a new price today.
In Indexa/Broadcast the runoff pair against Flávio Bolsonaro comes out 43% to 42%, a 1-point lead that fits inside the margin, that is, a statistical tie in that house.
candidates.analise: The two national polls of Sep 15 agree in putting him ahead in both rounds and disagree on by how much, and it is that disagreement the round measures. Indexa/Broadcast, by telephone, gives 4 points in the first round and 1 point in the runoff; CNT/MDA, in person, gives 10.1 and 7.3 points. Both declare the same margin of 2.2 and measured practically the same days, so the difference of 6.3 points in the runoff pair is between instruments, not between periods. In the market the day's move favours him: the winner contract rises 1.00pp, to 46.50% (vol USD 11.11M accumulated), and the gap to Flávio Bolsonaro narrows 1.30pp after widening for two days. The direction of the market and the direction of the two polls coincide today, which was not the case on Sep 14. The panel does not claim the market reacted to the polls: both measurements are from the same day and the order between them is not measured.

candidates.name: Flávio Bolsonaro
candidates.header: PRICE: 51.65% (vol USD 10.71M accumulated) in the winner contract, reading of Sep 15, 14:44 BRT, down 0.30pp against the price confirmed on Sep 14. POLLS: 34% in the first round and 42% in the runoff against Lula in Indexa/Broadcast of Sep 15, and 30.4% and 40% in CNT/MDA of the same day.
fortes: He remains ahead in the winner contract, with 51.65% against 46.50% for Lula.
In Indexa/Broadcast the runoff pair comes out 42% to 43%, a difference of 1 point that fits inside the margin of 2.2, so that house measures a statistical tie.
In the first-round runner-up contract his price did not move and stayed at 75.50%, and his share of that book rose, because Lula's side gave up 1.90pp.
In the first round of Indexa/Broadcast he stands at 34%, the same value as the house's previous wave, of Aug 26, while Lula gives up 1 point over the same interval.
fracos: He gives up 0.30pp in the winner contract and his gap to the runner-up narrows 1.30pp, from 6.45pp to 5.15pp.
He trails in both rounds in the two national polls of Sep 15, and in CNT/MDA both distances, of 10.1 and 7.3 points, fall outside two margins.
His price sits 3.45pp below the series high, of 55.10% on Sep 10, and has not come back to touch it in any reading since then.
candidates.analise: The round is one of a modest retreat in the market and of a deficit in both of the day's polls. In the winner contract he gives up 0.30pp, to 51.65% (vol USD 10.71M accumulated), and remains the favourite, but the gap to Lula narrows 1.30pp and undoes part of the widening of the two previous days. In the polls the reading depends on the house: Indexa/Broadcast puts him 1 point away in the runoff, inside the margin, and CNT/MDA 7.3 points away, outside it. The difference between the two is larger than the margin of each one, and the panel records both without choosing. In the first-round runner-up contract the distinction the panel always publishes applies: his price did not move a tenth, and his share of the book still rose, because the other side fell. A price standing still is not a position standing still.

candidates.name: Augusto Cury
candidates.header: PRICE: 0.45% in the winner contract, reading of Sep 15, 14:44 BRT, up 0.10pp. In the first-round third-place contract this round publishes no new price, and the value shown remains the 45.40% of Sep 14 (vol USD 197 thousand accumulated). POLLS: 6% in the first round in both national polls of Sep 15.
fortes: He has 6% in the first round in both national polls of Sep 15, the same value in both houses, and he is third in both.
In Indexa/Broadcast the runoff pair against Lula comes out 39% to 41%, a difference of 2 points that fits inside two margins of 2.2.
In the winner contract he rises 0.10pp, to 0.45%, and moves off his series floor, of 0.30% on Sep 10.
fracos: In CNT/MDA of Sep 15 he loses the runoff pair to Lula by 38.4% to 45.3%, a distance of 6.9 points that falls outside two margins.
In the winner contract the 0.45% sits 4.55pp below his series high, of 5.00% on Aug 27.
The first-round third-place contract, where he is the favourite, received no new reading on Sep 15, so his position there is yesterday's and not today's.
candidates.analise: The round measures stability in the polls and almost nothing in the market. The two national polls of Sep 15 put him at 6% in the first round, and the divergence between them shows up in the runoff pair: 2 points of deficit in Indexa/Broadcast, inside two margins, and 6.9 in CNT/MDA, outside them. In the winner contract he rises 0.10pp, to 0.45%, a small move in absolute terms that takes him off the series floor. In the first-round third-place contract, which is where he has a relevant price, this round publishes no new figure, because there was no new reading of it on Sep 15: the 45.40% (vol USD 197 thousand accumulated) is from Sep 14, and the panel says so instead of serving yesterday's price as if it were today's.

candidates.name: Renan Santos
candidates.header: PRICE: 1.60% (vol USD 13.49M accumulated) in the winner contract, reading of Sep 15, 14:44 BRT, down 0.10pp. In the first-round third-place contract this round publishes no new price, and the value shown remains the 37.50% of Sep 14 (vol USD 310 thousand accumulated). POLLS: 3% in the first round in Indexa/Broadcast of Sep 15 and 2.7% in CNT/MDA.
fortes: His contract is the one with the largest accumulated volume in the presidential book, at USD 13.49M, above the contracts of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro.
He has 3% in the first round in Indexa/Broadcast and 2.7% in CNT/MDA, and in both he is ahead of Romeu Zema.
In the first-round third-place contract he is second, with the 37.50% of Sep 14.
fracos: He gives up 0.10pp in the winner contract, to 1.60%, and sits 0.40pp from his series floor, of 1.20% on Aug 31.
He loses both runoff pairs to Lula outside two margins: 35% to 45% in Indexa/Broadcast and 33.9% to 47.3% in CNT/MDA.
In Indexa/Broadcast he falls from 4% on Aug 26 to 3% now, inside the house's margin.
candidates.analise: The round measures a small fall in the market and a wide deficit in the polls. In the winner contract he gives up 0.10pp, to 1.60% (vol USD 13.49M accumulated), and moves closer to the series floor, which is 1.20% on Aug 31. In the two national polls of Sep 15 he sits between 2.7% and 3% in the first round and loses both runoff pairs to Lula by more than ten points, outside two margins in both houses. The contrast the panel records is between volume and price: his contract accumulates more money than those of the top two and pays 1.60%. High volume measures interest accumulated since the book opened, not probability now.

candidates.name: Caiado / Haddad / Zema
candidates.header: PRICE: Ronaldo Caiado at 0.15% in the winner contract, stable, reading of Sep 15, 14:44 BRT; Romeu Zema at 0.15%, stable; Fernando Haddad at 0.05%, stable. In the first-round third-place contract this round publishes no new price, and the value shown for Ronaldo Caiado remains the 15.50% of Sep 14 (vol USD 130 thousand accumulated). caiado.fortes: He is fourth in the first round of Indexa/Broadcast of Sep 15, with 4%, and his runoff pair against Lula in that house comes out 39% to 43%, a distance of 4 points that fits inside two margins of 2.2.
caiado.fracos: In CNT/MDA of Sep 15 he falls to 3% in the first round and loses the runoff pair to Lula by 37.3% to 46.4%, 9.1 points that fall outside two margins. In the winner contract he stays at 0.15%, with no movement.

haddad.label: HADDAD (PT), 0.05% in the WINNER contract, confirmed reading of Sep 15, 14:44 BRT, at the floor of the book. He is not a presidential candidate: he is running for the government of São Paulo, and the two national polls of Sep 15 do not test him in a first-round presidential scenario.
haddad.fortes: His contract did not move in today's reading, so there is no movement to explain, and his series high in the winner contract is 7.60%, on May 26.
haddad.fracos: He is not measured in the first round by either of the two national polls of Sep 15, so the comparison between price and polling does not exist for him in this round.

zema.label: ZEMA (Novo), 0.15% in the WINNER contract, confirmed reading of Sep 15, 14:44 BRT, below the 0.5% floor of the double reading. In the first-round THIRD-PLACE contract this round publishes no new price. He has 1% in the first round in both national polls of Sep 15.
zema.fortes: He keeps 1% in the first round in both of the day's national polls, the same value in both houses, with no fall against their previous rounds.
zema.fracos: He loses both runoff pairs to Lula outside two margins, by 34% to 45% in Indexa/Broadcast and by 34.5% to 47.7% in CNT/MDA, with 11 and 13.2 points of deficit. In the winner contract he stays at 0.15%, and his series high is 12.00%, on May 13.

candidates.analise: The round does not move the three of them in the winner contract: Ronaldo Caiado and Romeu Zema stay at 0.15% and Fernando Haddad at 0.05%, the same values as the confirmed reading of Sep 14. In the polls, Ronaldo Caiado appears between 3% and 4% in the first round and Romeu Zema at 1% in both houses, and the divergence between the day's two national polls repeats in their pairs: Indexa/Broadcast puts Caiado 4 points from Lula, inside two margins, and CNT/MDA 9.1 points, outside them. In the first-round third-place contract, where Ronaldo Caiado had the strongest move on the panel on Sep 14, this round publishes no new price, because there was no new reading of it today.
fortes: Ronaldo Caiado is fourth in the first round of Indexa/Broadcast of Sep 15, with 4%, and his runoff pair against Lula in that house fits inside two margins.
Romeu Zema keeps 1% in both of the day's national polls, with no fall against the previous rounds of the same houses.
The three winner prices were stable in today's reading, with no movement to explain.
fracos: The three of them add up to 0.35% in the winner contract, and none of them goes above 0.15% individually.
Romeu Zema loses both runoff pairs to Lula outside two margins, with 11 and 13.2 points of deficit.
Fernando Haddad is not measured in the first round by either of the two national polls of Sep 15, so the comparison between price and polling does not exist for him in this round.

cruzamento: 📉 THE WINNER CONTRACT GAP NARROWED BY 1.30pp, AND BOTH SIDES MOVED: Lula rose from 45.50% to 46.50% (vol USD 11.11M) and Flávio Bolsonaro slipped from 51.95% to 51.65% (vol USD 10.71M), reading of Sep 15, 14:44 BRT, against the confirmed reading of Sep 14. The distance went from 6.45pp to 5.15pp, after two straight days of widening. Neither price is an extreme: the 51.65% sits 3.45pp below Flávio's series high, of 55.10% on Sep 10, and the 46.50% sits 21.00pp below Lula's high, of 67.50% on Aug 16. 🗳️ ON THE POLLING SIDE, TWO NATIONAL POLLS CAME OUT TODAY AND THE FINDING IS THE DISTANCE BETWEEN THEM. Indexa/Broadcast and CNT/MDA measured practically the same days, declare the same margin of 2.2pp and carry almost identical samples, of 2,000 and 2,002 interviews. Both put Lula ahead in both rounds, and the runoff gap is 1 point in one and 7.3 points in the other, a difference of 6.3 points between the houses. The difference between them is almost three times the declared margin of each one, so it is not explained by sampling alone: what changes is the instrument, telephone in one and in-person interviewing in the other. The panel records both without choosing. 🏛️ AND THE DAY'S THIRD AXIS IS INSTITUTIONAL: the Supreme Court plenary opened on Sep 15 the judgment on the investigation of Alexandre de Moraes, without concluding, and on the same day the contract that pays out if a Supreme Court justice leaves by impeachment before 2027 rose 2.80pp, to 8.05% (vol USD 91 thousand). It remains 18.05pp below the series high, of 26.10% on Sep 11, that is, it has recovered less than three points of the roughly twenty it lost between Sep 11 and Sep 14. It is a thin book, and a thin book moves on little money. The panel places the two measurements side by side and does not claim that one caused the other. 🔒 One contract on the panel receives no new price in this round: the first-round third-place contract had no new reading on Sep 15, and the values shown there remain those of Sep 14.
